page_note: Page 11 contains NO cosmological substrate. The entire page is ecclesial-apostolic discourse about Mani as 'the apostle' and his relationship to 'the church' (ⲧⲉϩⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ): how he comes in the flesh, oversees the church, departs upward, and leaves behind shepherds/helpers/guides (ⲣⲉϥⲭⲁⲩⲙⲁⲓⲧ used here for institutional guides, not the cosmic Pillar) for the church to continue. The second half develops parables (farmer, merchant, fruit-tree, harvest in winter/summer, month of Phaōphi) to which 'the apostles liken themselves.' These are application similes, not substrate cosmology. No five-fold mappings, no kings of the worlds, no zoomorphic correspondences. The chapter is Manichaean ecclesiology with hortatory/parabolic illustration. Damage ratio 91.9% — most segments are fragmentary, but the surviving content is uniformly ecclesial-apostolic. Editorial fatigue score (+0.27) reflects shift from ecclesial vocabulary in first half to apostolic/parable vocabulary in second half — both later layers, just different facets.
